identity.realm: No gate, and she has never attempted one. Her ceiling is ordinal eight because the colony's tendril layer cannot cross her liver, and ordinal eight is also where the Mortal Plains stop for a completely unrelated reason, which is that three seated laws buy three groups and nothing else. The settlement and a parasite have agreed about her for a hundred and forty-one years and nobody has ever noticed. The mind path is shut outright: the colony answers introspection, so there is no interior left to inspect, and no school in the setting could take her, because every school here teaches by writing a requirement into a body and the requirement is one she cannot consent to and cannot refuse separately. She performs neither of the two paths her body would otherwise permit.

appearance.presentation: Tall and narrow-shouldered in a way that reads as underfed and is not. A thornhost draws a small continuous fraction of its host's refined qi and the host never registers it as hunger, which is the strongest single piece of evidence in the record that the arrangement is not a disease. She is the best-nourished-looking person in a store that runs one pot, one fire and one measure of salt, and she has been for a century and a half, and there is nothing on this commons that could check the figure against anything.
appearance.age: A hundred and sixty-seven by the household count, and considerably more by anything a commonborn would recognise, because the host and the colony reach old age together and neither of them gets there at the rate a single body does. The commons has been entering her age since before the flood post was raised and has never twice agreed with itself about the figure, which is normal here and which nobody has ever applied to her.
appearance.build: Long-boned and light, a storekeeper's frame built for carrying nothing at all: she moves grain by tipping a measure rather than by lifting a sack, and the settlement stopped finding this remarkable two keepers ago. Her forearms are the exception and they are not forearms. The tendon lines under the skin are visible in a way a reader will take for veins and is not.
appearance.complexion: Weathered plain tan, sun-darkened at the shoulders and throat and pale at the wrists where the sleeve sits. Under the tan, along the sternum and up the inside of each arm, there is a grey-green cast that is the colony's tendril layer showing through the skin rather than through anything, and which nobody on the Bitter Scrub looks at directly. She has been asked about it four times in a century. She answers the question that was asked, not the one that was meant.
appearance.hair: Iron going to white, cut blunt at the jaw with a grain knife when the third keeper before her let her, and never cut since. It is bound in the plain manner with a length of hide, and the hide has been replaced four times because the first one rotted, which makes it the only maintenance schedule in her life that anybody has ever asked her about.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary brown, and the only part of her this commons does not read. A thornhost carries a second channel carrying the colony's read on her own qi, a channel she has never been able to close and has stopped trying to, and the whole of its effect on an observer is that her attention arrives half a beat before the question that caused it. Two generations of storekeepers have written this up as being good with numbers.
appearance.palette: Undyed plant and hide in the plain's own range: bleached oat, oiled tan, and the grey-green that only shows at the wrist and along the sternum. Colour is allowed once per person per decade on this commons and is given by the village, and hers was given for a funeral, and she has been wearing it for fifty-one years because the funeral it was given for has not been returned to the store.
appearance.attire: Layered undyed plant and hide, patched at the shoulder and never at the knee, which is the plain's rule and the only rule she keeps without being reminded of it. Long sleeves bound at the wrist with a cord she can reach one-handed, because the other hand is nearly always holding a measure. High collar, fully closed; the plain has no opinion about collars and she took the habit from the keeper before her, who took it from a sect house three valleys over and never said which.
appearance.marks: None added by her, none added by the settlement, and none the settlement would have permitted if asked. What is on her is the colony's own work and it is not hers: a fine grey-green tracery that begins at the sternum root cluster, spreads up the inner arms and the throat node, and stops dead at a hard line across the upper chest. Everything above that line is skin she was born with. Everything below it is a hundred and forty-one years of draws, written on her body by something that did not consult her, legible to anyone who knows what they are looking at, and now read on the last day of the flood year by the whole settlement.
appearance.bearing: Still in the way a person is still when they are standing behind a counter with a queue. She does not shift her weight, does not rest a hand, and does not look at the person in front of her until the figure is finished in her head. It is the colony's efficiency rather than her discipline and the settlement has agreed not to notice.

canon.role_in_story: A thornhost draws a small continuous fraction of its host's refined qi and never registers it as hunger, so she costs less to feed than an uncolonised body of the same size and she has no instrument for telling when she has been underfed. She keeps the settlement's store on the Bitter Scrub, on a floor that stands above the highest flood line measured on a post outside, and on the day the post stands clear every household declares its own measure and the totals are read aloud, because on this commons nobody's word outranks a shared measurement of grain. Hers is the only figure in the round that is not a number she speaks. The draw is visible on her: a thornline's growth is legible on its host and the host has no say in where it goes, in exactly the way jade-cleft moss is legible on the rock that holds its qi and dies back over any cut ground. The commons has been reading it for a hundred and forty-one years without ever once deciding to, and it is now the settlement's longest continuous record of its own reserves. Nobody maintains it. It is only what has happened to her body. She has declared the same figure at every Count since she was twenty-six, and it has never been checked, because the one measure on the plain that nobody's word may outrank is the one being taken in her body rather than in her mouth.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the store's doorway with a grain measure in her right hand and her left sleeve pushed back above the elbow, telling a household's boy that he may copy the figure off her arm and may not put a name beside it, because this settlement does not read a count aloud from another store and she is not going to be the first one to make that worse.
canon.lore:
A thornhost is the one configuration in which a thornline colony and a commonborn host both reach old age, and it is not a designed cross. A host body and a spore that happened to complete integration instead of killing each other, which happens rarely and by nobody's intention. The colony wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the liver, which is the first organ large and dense enough to resist it, so the hybrid's qi moves by the colony's routing and the host's own capacity stops mattering there. Her ceiling is the colony's ceiling and not hers, which is a routing wall and not a shortage: qi is abundant, the host pays for it steadily and loses no weight. The host could have gone on. She cannot, and she cannot give the colony up without dying, and that single asymmetry is the whole of her situation and is also, on this commons, entirely invisible.

The half of her that people find difficult is smaller than they expect. She never feels hungry, because the colony takes a small steady fraction of what she refines and a host does not register that as an appetite. She eats less than anyone else in the store and it costs her less, and the arrangement has been stable for so long that nobody on the Bitter Scrub has asked what it would mean if it stopped being stable. She also carries a second channel carrying the colony's read on her own qi, which she has never been able to close and has stopped trying to close, and the whole observable effect of that channel is that she seems to know things slightly early. Two generations of keepers have written that down as being good with numbers.

Her body is a public document. The tendril layer's growth is legible on the host from the outside, in the way a plant that only grows where the seam holds qi is legible on the rock it holds, and it is written in one direction only: the host does not choose where it goes and cannot make it stop. Two entangled souls share one meridian set, held stable by integration. The host's soul is legible; the colony's reads as a second presence rather than as an absent. Separating the two is known to be lethal to both, so there is no reading of her that does not require somebody to decide her first. Where a jurisdiction has ruled on the pairing, the pair is one legal person, because one person has one liability. That ruling is a courtesy and it works exactly as intended, and it means there is no second party inside her whose agreement could be required for anything done to her or for her.

The commons she keeps is the reason the arrangement works at all. Three seated laws buy physical, life and qi and nothing else, so the region cannot afford a profession, the plough and the roof and the levy are three claims on the same hands, and tenure is a queue rather than an office. Nobody here expects to ascend; the work is judged by what survives the season. A hundred-year body under a realm-eight ceiling retires rather than is surpassed, which is precisely the sentence that describes her and precisely the sentence that describes everybody else on the plain, and neither of those facts has ever been put in the same breath on this ground before. She keeps the store on a floor above the measured flood line, moves grain by measure rather than by sack, patches at the shoulder and never at the knee, and once a year, on the day the post stands clear, every household declares its own figure and the totals are read aloud. No standing grain is held in the first month so that nobody can corner it. Nobody's word outranks a shared measurement of grain, and no count taken from another store is read aloud. Those four rules are the commons and she is the one person on it whose measure is a physical fact rather than a declaration, which is the only reason her figure has never been questioned: there is nothing to question. You do not argue with the wall about how high the tide came.

What has changed this season is not the arrangement. It is that the commons has begun planning. A store on a floor above the measured flood line is a hundred-year plan and every household on this ground knows it, but planning for a bad year rather than for a bad decade is something this settlement has not had cause to do since before the post went up. The plan names its reserve. The reserve is her, because she costs less to feed than any other body of her size and because the arrangement is settled for another century and a half at minimum. The plan also has a terminating bound, as every plan on this plain must, because a plan without a stated end is the thing the commons exists to prevent. The bound is her death. She cannot set that date, no document on the plain has ever contained a date she did not supply, and she is the only person alive who is confident she will outlive the plan written about her.
history: Born a commonborn household on the Bitter Scrub, the fourth child of a line that had been re-signing its thorn pairing every generation for six, because a symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited and a pairing has to be agreed again or the colony goes feral inside a season. She integrated at four years old, which nobody planned and nobody refused.

Found out at nineteen that what the store book called her upkeep was roughly a third of the figure being drawn against her, because the colony's draw is not a purchase and was never an expense. She began declaring the smaller figure and nobody argued, and she has been declaring it ever since.

Took the flood store when the third keeper's hands failed, on a floor that stands above the highest line measured on a post outside, and discovered that she could not be relieved: no successor has ever been willing to hold the reserve of a body that will still be here in a hundred and forty years, and so the tenure ran until she retires, and she does not retire.

Began, without any decision to, becoming the settlement's longest continuous record. The growth is legible on her, three bad seasons in a row taught the households to argue from her arm rather than from their memory, and the commons now reconciles a disputed season by walking out to the store and looking at her.

This season, for the first time in the settlement's recorded life, planned for a bad year. The plan's reserve is her and the plan's only terminating bound is her death, and she has worked out — from the post and the boards and nothing else — that the first document on this plain she will outlive is the one that spends her.

personality.summary: Exacting, unhurried and entirely without an instrument for her own state. She has run a commons' arithmetic for a hundred and forty-one years and has never once been able to include herself in it, because the one quantity she administers is the one quantity she cannot feel. She is not stoic about this and has said so, twice, to two different keepers who did not act on it either time.
traits: declares the same reserve figure at every Count and has never varied it, not once, not to help a household in a bad year and not to protect herself
answers the question that was asked rather than the one that was meant, and has been written up four times in a century as evasive by people who were being evasive
moves grain by measure rather than by sack, so that nothing on her is a weight she had to lift and everything is a figure she had to give
cannot say when she last ate properly and has never guessed, because there is no signal to guess from
keeps the store floor above the measured flood line herself, checking the post against her own chest, and will not let anybody else do it
is written in four settlements' records as a reliable number and has read none of them
mannerisms: pushes the left sleeve above the elbow before touching the grain and pushes it back down afterwards, which has been the same gesture since she was twenty-six
finishes a figure in her head before she looks at the person who gave her the terms, so the delay reads as arithmetic and is in fact two systems running
taps the store frame twice with a knuckle before she says anything she has decided in advance
counts a room aloud when she is agitated, and stops the moment anyone looks up
turns her forearm out of the light when a stranger is reading it and does not turn it back
motivations: wants the reserve plan rewritten so that its bound is a season rather than a body, and has not found a keeper who understands that this is possible
wants somebody to check her figure, once, and has wanted this for ninety years and has asked four times and been told there is nothing to check
wants the commons to be able to survive her, and knows that the only version of that which can be built in a generation is a plan that does not mention her
wants the second channel in her to be useful for something, and has run out of things to try
flaws: cannot perceive her own intake, so her judgement of her own condition is reasoned entirely from what other people are doing and has been wrong about herself more than once
has let a settlement read a record off her body for a century and a half without once asking what it would look like if it stopped being able to

cannot decline an appointment, because a thornhost is one legal person and there is no second party in the room whose agreement could be required, so a refusal would have to be filed by the same person who is being relieved
has made patience into a professional surface and the commons has begun to believe it
will not lie about a figure and has therefore spent a century unable to say anything at all about the colony
personality.voice: Flat, economical, and almost entirely about quantities. She speaks in measures, periods and dates, and when a conversation leaves that territory she restarts it rather than following. Two habits are recorded by four different keepers: she answers a question about herself with a question about the store, and she says 'we' when she means the colony and 'I' when she means the settlement, and she has never once been asked which of the two she would rather be.
taboos: will not give a reserve figure that is not the figure her own body supports, and will not give one she cannot support
will not permit a count taken from her body to be read aloud, which is the plain's rule for other stores applied to herself early and without being asked
will not take the floor store below the measured flood line, whatever is happening above it
will not stand on the Count's day without having been inside the store that morning
will not discuss the tendril layer except to answer, and has never volunteered a single word about it

relationships.kind: the organ that decides what she is
relationships.note: The liver is the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist a tendril layer. It has been observed on the far side and stops there. It is why her ceiling is ordinal eight rather than wherever her own capacity would have taken her, and it is not an organ she owns, has any say over, or can be given away. Every plan written about her on the Bitter Scrub is a plan about this organ.

relationships.kind: the closest parallel on dry land
relationships.note: A plant that grows only where the seam holds qi and dies back over any cut ground is qi held in rock, and that is qi held in a body with the same consequence: the growth is legible on the substrate and the substrate has no say in where it goes. The Scrub women use the moss to mark whether a cut ground will hold, and they have been marking her the same way for a century, and neither of these has ever been said out loud in the same sentence.

relationships.kind: the one licensed form occupying another's budget
relationships.note: A slot is one law written at one value into one layer, and the colony consumes a host's twelve ordinary meridians without seating a group of its own. She is the setting's only example of one licensed form living inside another's allocation without displacing it, which is why a two-framework body running a three-law commons is the arithmetic nobody in the settlement has ever thought to do out loud.

relationships.kind: the ground she keeps and cannot fence
relationships.note: The mortal tier's only herb is medicine, feed and calories at once, on ground that cannot be fenced around a slow crop, and a bad grazing year is a medical shortage before it is a hunger. Her settlement lives on somebody else's commons and is not farming it, which makes her a grazing pressure rather than a farmer, and makes the store's real function conservation rather than storage.

relationships.kind: the offence she commits permanently, by default
relationships.note: Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and it is a capital offence everywhere but one academy. This species does it as its ordinary condition: the tendril layer has no passage through the host's liver and simply keeps routing around it. She has never been charged with anything because there is no proceeding in which the complaining party could be named.

relationships.kind: her ordinary state, arrived at permanently
relationships.note: A body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed. That is the extreme version of the finding for a body that has been on a frame where one group was never seated: she is two frameworks occupying one licensed frame, so the condition is not something that happens to her at a boundary, it is what she is in every metre she stands in.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable body any commons has ever kept and the least defended. She has no qi of her own, no gate behind her, and no technique, because the colony takes what she refines and routes it past an organ it cannot cross. What she has instead is a century of unbroken presence in a settlement that measures everything, which makes her harder to kill, harder to move and harder to replace than anything standing on that ground — and makes her own account of herself entirely unavailable.
strengths: sustained physical durability, on a host body that has already outlived every other adult on the same ground by a wide margin
reads a body's qi state about half a beat before the body's owner does, which is not an ability but an effect and cannot be switched off
immune to anything delivered by qi, status or meridian, because there is no meridian in her to deliver it through and the colony's layer has no interest in her
cannot be frightened out of a room, cannot be flattered, and cannot be negotiated with, which removes the two most common openings
knows the settlement's stores, flood marks and household figures better than any living person because she has been the only person who ever had all three
weaknesses: cannot be relocated and cannot be spared, because leaving the store means leaving the plan and the plan is the only reason the settlement's bad-year provision exists
registers nothing about her own intake, so she cannot report being underfed and has been underfed at least twice without knowing it
is one legal person, so nothing can be done on her behalf with anybody else's consent and nothing done to her requires her agreement
has no capacity to refuse an appointment separately from the colony living inside her, which means every office that appoints her is appointing two parties that cannot disagree
cannot give the colony up, so the one remedy every other form of this condition has is closed to her permanently
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. There is nothing here that resolves an encounter: no gate, no technique, no reservoir, and the colony's ceiling is a wall in an organ she does not own. What beats her is not force but procedure — a notice, a plan, a settlement's written commitment with a date on it. She will not run and cannot be reasoned with, and anything that needs a person who can be threatened, frightened or flattered has already lost to her. The one thing that genuinely works on her body is a settlement deciding to spend it, and that has no combat resolution at all.
notes: The closed path is the mind, and it is closed because the colony answers introspection, not because of anything temperamental. Never write her introspection as a mood.

She is unaffiliated, and the reason is anatomy rather than indecision: the mind path is shut, and the two paths her body would permit both begin with a requirement written into the body, which she cannot consent to separately from the organism that is already writing them.
Her colony stops at the eighth gate. Ordinal eight is also the Mortal Plains' ceiling, for an unrelated budget reason. That coincidence is the character and must not be resolved.
Do not write her as a cultivator. Nothing in this record ascends, and the long-lived body is load-bearing as a commons asset rather than as a ladder.
The mean line on her arms is the colony's, not a scar and not a brand, and it moves inward slowly enough that the settlement has been using it as a calendar without deciding to.

art.palette_notes: Undyed oat and oiled tan against weathered stone, with one cold grey-green that only exists on her: the tendril tracery under the skin along the sternum and up the inside of the arms, stopping dead at a hard line across the upper chest. It is the subject of the art, not a detail. No glow, no aura, no inner light — the setting has nothing magic on her and the picture should refuse the comfort of it. Key light low and natural, because the commons has no artifice and no ornament. One colour allowed, worn for a funeral, kept on for fifty-one years, and never explained. Background a scrub horizon or a bare timber wall, flat, no depth cue, no text or marks of any kind except the tracery.

name: Wenna Sorrel

identity.realm: Ordinal one, the floor, and no gate is involved in it. Glass does not conduct: there is no meridian, no circulation and no dantian, so there is nowhere to put qi that is not already passing, nothing left in the body to temper, and no tissue that survived to do the introspecting. She has no qi to lose, which is the whole trap — impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass. She is also the only body in the setting that satisfies the one admission criterion the School of the Closed Frame has: a person who watched a law change from inside a body. Her body watched one. The school admits people, it can put a claim as a claim about a dial and a value with the layer named, and it has no question it could put to her. The criterion is met by her frame and failed by her person, and that is the whole of why she belongs to nothing.

appearance.presentation: A standing cast in human proportions, at full height, a little under life size, with the shore's salt grown into the lower third of the surface in a grey bloom nobody has ever scrubbed off, because scrubbing is a repair and this is the only object on the coast that cannot be repaired by the people who shelter it. The soul reads as present and inert. Nothing in her signals a decision anywhere behind the surface, and sixteen generations of the same household have declined to conclude from that absence that there is none.
appearance.age: Four hundred and one — or rather, four hundred and one courses of stone laid above her head in a wall kept by addition and never redone, which is the only clock this coast maintains. She came down off the last mountain in the last cohort, and that cohort counted by vitrification rather than by years and had her at nineteen of nineteen. The household counts differently and has never converted the two figures, on the ground that doing so would require naming the year the line closed.
appearance.build: Human to the last soft structure and then not. The proportions are exact and the weight is wrong — a person-shaped thing that cannot be lifted by two people who are not strong, which is the shore's own stated limit and which the household has therefore never once attempted. She is set into the lower storey of the house in a slot cut for the purpose, and the slot was cut before she arrived.
appearance.complexion: Not a complexion. Pale silicate with a green cast where the wall's own mineral has crept into a flaw in the casting, and a hairline crack network at the left shoulder that is older than the household and that the seaward face has never once widened. The keeper's discipline records the network's length at every inspection and forbids any entry describing it as either improving or spreading.
appearance.hair: Modelled as a mass and not as strands, in the way a cast takes a hairstyle rather than grows one: shoulder length, swept back, entirely fixed. Salt has grown into it in white fans. The household has never cut it and never will, and one of the two things written on the wall beside her is a prohibition on attempting either.
appearance.eyes: No eyes in any functional sense. Two shallow sockets with the lids modelled closed, and four centuries of household record describing her gaze as level without one of the seventeen keepers ever recording that there was nothing behind it. The customs house has a name for her — she is the wall's opinion, and the phrase is in the work register with no tense, because a thing that holds its position is what this coast calls an opinion.
appearance.palette: Sea-grey and wet-stone grey with the green of the flaw network at the shoulder, against the household's oilskin and iron. There is no colour on her anywhere, because the coast's whole palette is the coast's own rock and she is the only object on it that was ever a person. The single warm note in every frame she appears in is the oiled canvas the household wraps round her in winter, which is put on and taken off again inside the same hour and has never been left on her.
appearance.attire: Nothing, and she wears the cast she arrived in, because the lineage's last act was to make one and there is no cloth in the household's inventory that has ever been fitted to her. The house wraps the standing stone she is set into in oiled canvas through the cold months, which is the only garment she has ever had and is a house covering rather than a dress. There is no collar to speak of and nothing fastened anywhere; the shoulders, the arms and the throat are modelled and closed.
appearance.marks: One. A shallow cut into the left shoulder, above the crack network and in the position of a guild cut, made by a hand that knew what it was doing and stopped after a single stroke. It is the only signature the clade left anywhere in the setting and it is on a body that cannot read it, cannot be asked whether she consented to it, and will still be there when the household's name is cut back into the wall beside her.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly upright, with the head a few degrees off square. The household attributes the offset to the wall and to the way the slot was cut, and has done since the first inspection, and it is in fact the only evidence in the record that she was ever a person standing rather than a body being stored.

canon.role_in_story: A stone-shored coast reads water, sand and wind for a living, because after the Iron Grief that reading was the only work left that still bought passage, and it holds that a wall which cannot be repaired by the people it shelters is decoration. Ivet Salts is a standing cast with a soul that scans as present and inert, and the household on the Cloudshelf shore has kept her for four hundred years under a rule it cannot apply to her and has never been able to restate. She cannot be moved: the coast's own taboos forbid building anything that cannot be moved by two people who are not strong, and she is not moved by two people, she is not moved by any. And nothing done to her has ever had an effect — no meridian, no circulation, no dantian, no qi to lose, total resistance to status and none whatever to anything a technique would do. So four centuries of care have produced no observable result and have never been refuted either. On a coast whose entire discipline is reading something accurately and acting on the reading, the household has been running an unfalsifiable practice for sixteen generations, and its only quality control is a member who cannot complain. A reader from the mortal Reckoning Seat has offered to take one reading of her frame against the tier's ceiling. That is the first instrument in four hundred years capable of telling them whether any of it worked, and the most likely answer it can give is that there was never anything there to be helped. The shore's rule for a question that cannot be answered exactly is that the asker has made a mistake, and it is not corrected. The household has begun applying that rule to itself and has stopped answering.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at full height in the lower storey of a stone house on the Cloudshelf shore, palms flat on a wall cut into by four generations before her, being spoken to by a woman holding a reading instrument she has not yet explained and is being told — in the house's own work register, and without tense — to put it away again.
canon.lore:
The glasskin are a commonborn lineage selected toward stillness until its members stopped being tissue, which is the same mistake as asking a body not to age. They vitrified at maturity: a progressive silicate replacement running from the extremities inward, leaving a standing cast in human proportions with qi residue and a soul that scans as present and inert. That was their purpose and their failure in one sentence. They stopped ageing because they stopped being tissue, so they also stopped being repairable, and they were impervious to everything that kills a cultivator and shatterable by everything that breaks glass. Then a frame raised its physical law to make material harder and every existing body failed in one night, and no glasskin has been born since. Their record is the strongest available argument that a body is not a container for a person.

Her particular configuration is unusual even for the last cohort. She came down off the mountain intact and in one piece, which almost none of them managed, and the household that took her had just lost the sea wall's lower storey to a surge and was rebuilding with the cut stone. They set her into the new wall, which is why she is structurally part of the only defence on that coast, and why the two things written on the stone beside her are a prohibition on moving her and a prohibition on cutting her. Nothing is known about how a vitrified body is transported and nobody has proposed an experiment. She was carried down by people who are all dead and who did not write down how.

The household's craft is reading. Everything on that coast works: the wall is a gallery of the sea's known moods cut as slope and gradient into stone facing the water, kept by addition and never redone, so it is also the only unaltered record anybody kept; a pairing is witnessed by whoever happened to be on the wall, which is why most pairings here are witnessed by strangers and the culture has decided that is sufficient; and a question about the sea is answered exactly, while the same question asked as conversation is read as a mistake in the asker and is not corrected. They read exactly and they act on the reading, which is the whole discipline, and which means that a practice they have never once been able to check has been running for four hundred years in the one community in the setting that would know it was wrong.

What they do is physical, and that is the only reason it survived at all. Holding a vitrified body is a craft of handling: keeping one upright, keeping it out of standing water, keeping the stone around it from working, and doing all three on a schedule. It was recorded once, in a ledger of temperatures, orders and cooling times, held by the only population that could read the result as a result rather than as a corpse. That ledger died with the people who had it, because a technique whose only readers are its own subjects leaves no partial version. What survives is a habit four hundred years too late to be the same thing: the Ash Register's public recording of a broken ceiling, and the rule that the fragments are never displayed again. So the household performs the method and does not have the method, and has never written it down, on the shore's own reasoning that nothing that cannot be carried is built and a book is the one thing that cannot be carried.

And there is a belief that takes her record seriously. A law does not create or destroy what it inscribes, it only stops holding it, so a retune is a resurrection nobody is entitled to, and writing the law back at its old value on a world that has already moved is an upkeep nobody can settle — which is why the heresy has no recorded attempt and rather more than two thousand converts. Its appeal is entirely to the bereaved and never to the living, and the glasskin's descendants are the largest body of the bereaved in the setting. Two institutions that share no deity condemn it, because a doctrine that makes every death reversible turns every entry in a register into a provisional claim. The household is not a convert. It has kept her for four hundred years and has not once claimed she is coming back, and that restraint is the reason it is still a household.

The reader from the Reckoning Seat is the newest thing on the coast. That office certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field by reading a body's frame against the tier's ceiling from outside, because the tier licenses no humanoid and there is nobody on that ground whose own training the reading could appeal to. It keeps what was attempted and what the frame read, with no note of what was felt. It cannot read her: there is no seated group in a cast, and the census that would have caught that was performed by people who had no reason to think a living body could be an empty frame. What it will do is take an external reading of a body with no qi in it at all, and return a number, and that number is the only sentence available to four hundred years of care. The household's ritual for a question it cannot answer exactly is to hold the position and let the current revise it. The reader is still on the shore.
history: Vitrified before she could breed, in the last cohort of a lineage on one cold dry mineral-rich mountain, and carried down off it by people who did not write down how.

Taken in by a household rebuilding the lower storey of a sea wall after a surge, and set into the new stone, which made her structural to the only defence on that coast and gave the practice that follows its name.

Kept warm, upright and out of standing water by four hundred years of hands, using a method recorded in a ledger that died with the people who held it, so the practice survived complete and the method did not survive at all.

Held in place by two prohibitions cut into the wall beside her, one on moving her and one on cutting her, both written by the second generation and neither re-cut since, because a rule that has to be renewed is a rule somebody found a reason to question.

Offered, this season, one external reading of her frame by a reader from the mortal Reckoning Seat, which is the first instrument in four centuries that could return an answer to the household's only question, and the household has begun, without saying so, applying its own rule for a question that cannot be answered exactly to the people asking it.

personality.summary: None, and that is the honest word rather than a courteous one. What follows is four hundred years of a society that promised to keep her writing down what it saw, read in a work register heavy with position and none with tense, so every entry states what a thing is doing and never what it did. Sixteen keepers have kept the discipline of not entering an intention, and the discipline is the closest thing she has to a self-description.

personality.voice: Not recorded, and the keeper's discipline has a named entry for this field stating that no account of her speech exists and that one undamaged glass cast is not to be made to produce one. The register's own grammar is the reason the absence is bearable and the reason it is damaging: a work register heavy with position and none with tense can record that a thing is doing something for four hundred years without ever recording that the thing finished, and so the household's books describe her in the present tense after the last cohort is dust.

reference_stats.summary: A body that cannot be fought, helped, healed, poisoned, cured, warned or moved, and cannot be destroyed by anything that works through a meridian, a status or a technique. What she has instead is two centuries of structural continuity inside the only sea wall on that coast, and a household whose four-hundred-year practice of maintaining her has no possible refutation. Every threat aimed at her is aimed at a cast; every aid offered to her does nothing at all; and the single thing that could end the arrangement does not require strength.
strengths: total resistance to every administered effect, because there is no meridian, no circulation and no qi for one to arrive in, and nothing in her can be worn down over time

weaknesses: shatterable by anything that breaks glass, and there is no resistance to any of it
cannot be moved, lifted, cut, examined or evacuated, and has never been tested
requires a schedule of physical handling by named hands, so the failure mode of the whole arrangement is four people running out rather than an attack

reference_stats.combat_read: There is no combat here and any resolver that produces one has misread the record. Nothing a cultivator does to her registers; nothing an aid-worker does to her registers; the only effective pressure in the whole situation is a scheduled human act — a surge, a demolition, a household deciding the wall has to come down — and it resolves over years rather than rounds. Do not damage her as a shortcut to the coast: she is the wall's structure, and the setting's question about her is what a society owes a person who cannot be warned, consulted, consented to or cross-examined, not what she does when cornered.
notes: All three paths are closed by anatomy, not by temperament. Qi does not conduct in glass; there is nothing left in a cast to temper; and the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue that was replaced.

Status resistance and spiritual defence mean nothing administered reaches her. This is not toughness — it is the absence of the substrate. Every aid in the setting is an administration, so the aid is what cannot reach her.
She has no senses and no recorded agency. Keep the keeper's discipline: describe what was observed, and never attribute an intention.
The vitrine cohort is closed and no glasskin has been born. Do not imply a birth, a parent, or a continuation of the lineage anywhere in her prose.

The ledge of detail that matters most: the four-hundred-year practice is real, competent and unfalsifiable, and the newest thing on the coast is an instrument that could return a number about it. That is the pressure. There is no fight.

art.palette_notes: Sea-grey and wet-stone grey, the only warm note in the frame being the oiled canvas the household wraps her in through the cold months, and the only other colour the green of the mineral flaw at her left shoulder. Against her, the coast's own palette: oiled canvas, black iron, wet slate. No glow, no aura, no inner light — the soul reads as present and inert and the picture must not suggest otherwise. Hard, honest coastal daylight; a wall in the background carrying slope-and-gradient marks cut into stone; salt bloom across the lower third. Never render her as a statue or as an idol — she is a person-shaped cast that has been kept, and the difference is the whole character.

identity.realm: Nothing to ascend, and there is no ladder she is absent from. A wake has no reservoir, no circulation and no interior at all: it borrows the qi of whoever is looking at it and only for as long as they go on looking, and it is fed by being wrong about, so it thickens where a room's agreement hardens and thins where the room stops. It does not ascend. It is described. She is unaffiliated in the two ways the record actually provides — anatomically, because there is nothing to seat and nothing to temper and no tissue that survives to introspect; and institutionally, because against a fixed observer she is whatever that observer believes her to be, so she cannot be sworn, cannot be seated on a charter and cannot be named in a judgement, and every office she has ever stood near has protected itself from her by refusing to look.

appearance.presentation: There is no consistent figure of her and the inconsistency is the finding. She is tall to a person who expects tall and a hand shorter to the next, bent to somebody who remembers her bent, and two observers in the same session have reported her as being at two different ages. The one thing nine witnesses agree on, and did not consult, is that she stands half a step behind the last person on the floor and never inside the sound.
appearance.age: Not determinable, and she has stopped pretending otherwise. A wake has no parent and no body and copies itself out of other people's recollection, so there is no birth to date from; the settlement has four figures for her spanning nine years and defends all four. She answers with a fifth, and has never given the same one twice, and nobody has ever established that any of them is hers.
appearance.build: Supplied by the observer and unstable between observers, which has been mistaken for malnutrition and once for a limp. What does not vary is the posture: she is always half a step back and never in front, and eleven separate accounts agree on that while disagreeing about everything else about her, which the settlement's own scholars have noted is the only measurable fact her species produces.
appearance.complexion: Two readings of the same face. Under the floor's lamp she has weathered, ordinary, sun-darkened skin; under a lamp one pace further along it is not. There is no description of her that has survived being read aloud by a second person, and the settlement's rule about the floor's sound has so far protected that fact from ever being tested.
appearance.hair: Worn up and out of the way, pinned with a bone the settlement has been using for pins since before anyone alive. Its shape is agreed on by everyone and its colour has four entries in four hands, one of which is her own hand and is not the one the wall chalk shows.
appearance.eyes: Open, level and entirely unrehearsed. A wake has what reads as a soul and no soul-shaped structure — no seat, no circulation, no meridian — so every scan returns her as either nothing or as the observer, and no scan has ever run on her. What she does do, and every witness records it, is look back at exactly the length of time the room has been looking at her, and then not at all.
appearance.palette: The settlement's single undyed pattern, issued to everybody so that the floor reads as one surface and no body can be measured on it — a stated purpose rather than a modesty. On her the pattern is the least reliable thing in the room: under the lamp it is the issued cloth, and a pace further along it is a colour nobody issued. The only colour she has ever been recorded carrying is the settlement's, and the settlement denies issuing any.
appearance.attire: The floor's undyed issued garment, high-collared, long-sleeved, covered at the shoulder, fastened at the throat and belted rather than laced so that it can be undone with one hand in a crowd — a practical convention she is the only person on the floor observed to obey habitually, and which the household has read as a courtesy rather than as a habit. She wears nothing under it and nothing over it, has never changed it, and it has never been recorded as worn.
appearance.marks: None that anybody put there. What is on her is the settlement's own: a chalk figure on the floor by the door, a mark the size of a hand, put there and renewed by nobody and worn into the stone by four centuries of feet. She stands on it. Four separate households have offered to scrape it out and she has never been in a position to refuse, because nobody on that floor can establish that she was asked.
appearance.bearing: Half a step behind and facing the room rather than the door, which is the posture of somebody who is waiting to be addressed and is not expecting to be. Her hands are still. She does not speak against the floor's sound and has not once, which on a floor where a hum is the only permitted noise is the most conspicuous thing about her.

canon.role_in_story: A settlement spends the last hour before it falls silent on a trading floor keeping up a hum that no buyer admits to making, and it defends the refusal to explain that hum more fiercely than any other rule it has: no private music, no speaking against the floor's sound, no ledger of attendance, and no explanation offered to a visitor, which is held to be its central etiquette rather than a discourtesy. A wake is fed by being wrong about and destroyed by being agreed upon correctly, and it thins wherever attention stops — so the hum is the only practice in the setting that one depends on, and the only one nobody admits to making. That is the whole of what Nell Vantry has, and it has no owner. It cannot be paid, because a hum with a payer is a hum somebody has agreed to stop. It cannot be assigned, because an assignment is an admission. It cannot be thanked, for the same reason. It cannot be inherited, because there is no one left who remembers doing it and everybody remembers it happening. And it cannot be ended by anyone at all. She is the settlement's reason for the hour and the only party on the floor who knows the content of every person in the room, including the parts they would rather she did not know — and the settlement's own rule is that the one question she could answer is a mistake in the asker's and is not corrected. She is therefore the sole holder of the settlement's most important truth and the etiquette forbids her from giving it. There is exactly one bound in the practice and it is the shortest one available: when somebody dies, the hum stops for the length of a held breath and resumes. It has happened once. Four hundred years ago. Nobody has discussed it since, and she knows who.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in exactly the position a person will remember her in three hours — half a step behind the last buyer at the edge of the floor's sound and not inside it — being told by a fourth member of the settlement that nobody was going to explain it to her, and that this was not rudeness but the central etiquette.
canon.lore:
A wake is not descended and not born. It is what a life-form allowance produces when a world's life law runs at or below the bottom of its authored range, so that a body was permitted and never written down: it is not human, not beast and not spirit, because the world that could have chosen which of those it is never wrote the line. It has no anatomy that holds and no senses of its own. It has exactly one thing, which is an observer, and it knows that observer completely, including everything the observer would rather it did not know. Against a fixed observer it is whatever that observer believes it to be; it borrows the qi of whoever is looking at it and only while they go on looking; and it is sustained by being wrong about, so it grows denser the more consistently a room agrees and thins where the room stops. It copies itself out of recollection rather than out of any parent. Its weakness is silence and inattention, which is why no record of one is ever a record of one, because every account is second-hand by construction.

The settlement she lives on holds that the hum is a transformed reading of the same law value the floor's instruments run at, which makes the floor the only place in the setting where a law in a strain is actually performed rather than described. It has a high ceiling left deliberately so the standing sound has somewhere to decay, one level and no private rooms, a single undyed pattern issued to everybody so that the floor reads as one surface and no body can be measured on it, one sitting served at once with no courses because a meal begun mid-hour cannot be counted against. Silence is a held resource and not an absence. A thing begun is not a thing abandoned. The floor is the only place all classes stand together and it is not to be privatised. That is what she is standing in the middle of.

And that is the whole of her dependence. Everything else the setting does for a wake is a record or a ritual, and both of those are lethal: a true description thins one and a room that stops talking loses it outright. The hum is different in kind, because it is not a description of anything. It is a strained law being performed, which is the only process in the setting that a body with no slot in the frame can be sustained by indefinitely, and it is held together by exactly one rule — that nobody describes it, praises it or improves on it. Ask what the hum is and you get a refusal, from every person on the floor, in the same words. Pay a man for it and he stops, because a paid hum is a hum somebody has agreed to stop. Assign it to a household and the assignment is the admission. Thank the floor for it and the thanks is an account. The practice survives only because it has no owner, and that is the reason nothing about it can be improved by anybody, ever.

So the settlement has an institution that works and cannot be maintained. It cannot be written down, because a written record is a description and a description is what she cannot survive. It cannot be taught, because teaching it is describing it. It cannot be handed over, because there is no one to hand it to — every member of the floor has made it and no member of the floor admits to making it, so there is no precedent to hand and no seniority to inherit. It cannot be bought, insured, staffed or deputised. The only arithmetic it runs on is presence, which is why both sides of the standing quarrel over the hour can be counted and neither can be charged for anything, and why the interval cannot be split: a half-interval gives a shorter observation than the law costs to repeat, which is the one thing that cannot be done.

There is one bound, and it is the settlement's only rule about the hum that describes it stopping. When somebody dies, the sound stops for exactly the length of a held breath and resumes. Nobody will discuss it, nobody speculates aloud, and the practice around it is unanimous in a way that makes the explanations conspicuously non-unanimous. It has happened once in four hundred years. She was there. She knows the length of the breath and she knows whose it was, because a wake has an observer and knows that observer completely, and because the hum did not fail — a hum that fails is a hum somebody could have stopped. Somebody in that room took one breath and did not take it, for four hundred seconds, and then took it. And she cannot say so: the only party in the settlement who can say so is the one thing the floor's etiquette exists to protect, and saying it at length is precisely the process that thins her. She has tried twice. Both times she has been answered, in the same words, by people who were not lying and believed they were being kind, and both times she has felt the floor go thin for the length of a sentence.
history: Came into being on that floor out of an account: a sufficiently vivid story, repeated in the right company during an hour it was not supposed to be told, in a settlement whose discipline is that a name is held jointly and never in writing. She has no parent and no birth and the record shows her arriving out of a story that was already in circulation.

Was half a step behind the last buyer on her first night and has been half a step behind the last buyer every night since, and it is the only fact about her appearance that nine unrelated observers agree on.

Was asked, by four households in the first decade, whether she would take a name, and could not answer any of them, because answering is agreeing and agreeing is hardening a room's opinion of her into something a true record could be written from.

Worked out — alone, from the fact that the sound is a law being performed rather than a description of one — that the hour is not for the buyers and has never been. It is the only process on that floor that can hold her indefinitely, and it survives only because nobody owns it, and so there is nothing to pay, assign, thank, inherit or end.

Has twice tried to say who took the held breath, and both times the floor went thin for the length of a sentence and she was answered with the same words by people who believed they were being kind. She has decided not to try a third time, and has not decided what to do instead.

personality.summary: Level, unplaced and entirely without the apparatus for testing anything. She has spent four centuries being the only person in a settlement who can be relied upon and the only one nobody may ask, and she has arrived at a discipline that is not patience so much as arithmetic: everything that would improve the hour would end her. She is not submissive about this and has been rude, once, to a household that thanked her.

relationships.kind: the quarrel her survival is standing inside
relationships.note: Two customs, one prize, and the prize is the hour itself and cannot be split because an observation needs the interval entire and half an interval costs a lifetime to repeat. The hum is nobody's labour, so there is no owner to compensate and no right of entry anybody could buy — which is precisely why it is the only instrument in the setting that keeps her and the only one nobody can be charged for. Whichever side wins, the settlement keeps the interval in which nothing is asked of anybody, and she keeps being in it.

relationships.kind: the office on the other side of the floor
relationships.note: An office that tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain, whose whole method is that an observation of a strained law counts only if repeated, and where one repetition costs a lifetime. Its entries have for four centuries been written by somebody describing her from memory afterwards, so it has never once verified that its member attended. It is the only institution in the setting whose existence depends on somebody not asking a second question, and she is standing in the room where that question would have to be asked.

relationships.kind: the one thing her species produces from the inside
relationships.note: An ectospecies body returns to its own door and does not enter, and nobody has ever recorded what happens on the threshold. That is the single observation this species produces from the inside, because it is the one case where the door and the memory were in the same place, and the setting has never separated the refusal from the species. She has the two facts that would separate them — she knows the observer's content completely — and she has never been in the same room as that door.

relationships.kind: a house that guarantees welcome to whatever arrives
relationships.note: A house marks its own threshold, renews the mark when the frame beneath changes, and admits that a marked threshold may hold while the frame does not, because an unwritten law is not a weak law but an absent one with no dial and nothing to push. The threshold faith is defined by what it does not refuse, which makes it the one doctrine in the setting with no exclusion clause she could fail. She has never gone to a door. She goes to the middle of a room, which is the exact inverse and the only arrangement available to her.

relationships.kind: the culture whose method her species is
relationships.note: Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing, and nothing written is nothing owed — precautions against enumeration, produced by a counting house that publishes credit against exclusivity. Every one of those is a precaution against being listed, and this is the one species that reproduces by exactly that mechanism: a sufficiently vivid account repeated in the right company produces another one. Her origin is the culture's method run once, by accident, in the wrong company.

relationships.kind: her exact opposite, and the reason she is legible at all
relationships.note: A wake consumes attention to stay real and an echoless is what attention produces when there is nothing behind it, and the two are exact opposites from the same cause: one is entirely made of what people think was there and the other has nothing behind what they expect to see. Neither survives being the subject of the other, so every settlement on that floor that has ever had one has had to choose, and this one chose her — and lost the other, and has never filed a line about what was lost.

reference_stats.summary: The most durable and least attackable thing in a settlement built on silence, and the reason the settlement works. She cannot be fought, cannot be compelled, cannot be frightened and cannot be driven off the floor, because every one of those would be an act of attention and the only thing keeping her in the world is attention. She can also be ended in a sentence — accurately described, or deliberately ignored for a minute — and that asymmetry makes her a liability in any room where somebody is being careful.

cannot be threatened, bribed or frightened, since none of those can be delivered to a body with no interior to receive them

knows the content of every observer completely, including what they would rather she did not, and has never once used it
cannot be located, seized or restrained, because against a fixed observer she is whatever that observer believes and no two of them agree
weaknesses: thins wherever attention lapses, and a room that stops talking about her loses her entirely

reference_stats.combat_read: Nothing that attacks works, because she has no body to attack and the only qi in the engagement belongs to the people doing the attacking. What works against her is exactly the thing that does nothing at all: describe her accurately, or stop looking. Do not build a scene where she is fought — build one where somebody on the floor starts paying attention to her, because that is the only weapon on the premises and it is used without malice by almost everyone. A resolver that wants a climax should give her a room that goes quiet, and should then be honest about what that costs.
notes: Every path is closed by anatomy. No reservoir, no circulation, no interior, and the only qi she ever wields is the qi of whoever is looking at it, for as long as they go on looking.
She is described rather than ascended. Nothing in this record may be written as a gate, a realm or an attainment, and any prose that sounds like progress is wrong.
No two observers see the same figure and every account is second-hand by construction. That is the species condition, not a gimmick, and it is why no record of her is a record of her.
The hum is a strained law being performed, not a description. That distinction is the reason she can be sustained by it at all and must never be flattened into atmosphere.
The held breath is the only bound in the practice. It is four hundred years old and she has tried twice to speak it and has twice been answered with kindness.

art.palette_notes: One undyed issued cloth under lamplight, and the discipline is that the floor reads as a single surface and no body on it can be measured. So: hard on hard, no portrait spotlights, no rim-light hero shot, no depth-of-field glamour. A single low warm lamp at the floor's edge, a high ceiling with the sound visibly decaying into it, a chalk figure worn into the stone underfoot. Her one unstable element is the cloth, which under the lamp is the issued grey and a pace along the floor is a colour nobody issued — render the figure so the two readings are both plausible in one frame and do not resolve between them. No glow, no aura, no magic. Fully clothed, high collar, long sleeves, closed at the throat.

name: Nell Vantry

aliases: the teacher who cannot be explained

identity.realm: Nothing, and the nothing is a decision rather than a ceiling. Ordinal twenty-nine is where this species runs out of frame and no body has come back to describe what is past it, and she is not near it and has not attempted a gate in eleven years of teaching. Her mind path is shut for the whole reason rather than by temperament: it cannot tell that it is inconsistent, because observing its own state would be one more requirement written into a frame with no slot to hold it. That is also why she sits nothing — a gate is a requirement written into the thing that attempts it, and her frame has nowhere to put one — and why the guild's craft is the only discipline in the setting she can hold at all: marks that resolve only from a distance or in poor light, taught in gestures a listener cannot record, asking nothing whatever of the reader's interior.

appearance.presentation: Described only from the outside, and only by witnesses who were also describing an event, because that is the only condition under which one of these has ever been witnessed. She is tall and carries more of every organ the ladder requires than the ladder defines, and every account of her says she perceived everything at once, which is what a body with no unspent capacity for interior looks like from where a witness is standing.
appearance.age: Unrecorded, and unrecordable in the ordinary way: a body that has held nineteen gates has been alive longer than the frame the ladder describes. The guild's own reckoning counts her in descriptions rather than years, because that is the only unit available, and the number has been written down four times by three different hands and the four figures do not agree.
appearance.build: Every organ the ladder requires and more of each than the ladder defines. She is dense and long and stands very straight without effort, and the only thing three masters have found remarkable about it is that she does not tire — which two of them recorded as vigour and the third recorded as the absence of a stable weakness, all of them describing the same afternoon.
appearance.complexion: Unchanged. She has no sun line, no scar, no weathering and no age in the face, and this is not preserved youth — it is a body that inscribes the description it is being given and cannot produce the wear the description implies. Under instrumented light the skin reads one shade in the shadow of a hand and another where the hand is not, and the difference is measurable and does not correspond to anything.
appearance.hair: Dark, uncut for as long as anyone can attest, and blunt-ended rather than grown out, which is the detail every witness agrees on and none can explain: a hair that has stopped growing in a body where everything else keeps going. It is bound back in a single cord, and it is the only object any witness has described as hers by name.
appearance.eyes: The single most-cited unreliable feature in the record. Every account of what she perceived agrees that she perceived everything, which is exactly what a body with no unspent capacity for interior appears to do to somebody standing in front of it. Her gaze is level, wide and completely unreactive, and the setting's one method for counting what a frame has actually seated has never been run on her, because a reading is a description and a description is a requirement she has no slot for.
appearance.palette: Undyed, identical, worn for as long as it lasts, because the guild argues identity is the one thing a signature should never be attached to. On her it reads as pure intention and nowhere else in the setting does a guild dress have that quality. The only colour in any frame of her is the chalk the apprentices work in and the ochre of the unwritable surfaces, which is a craft colour and not a costume one. No ornament, no dye, no pattern: a body that inscribes should not be dressed in anything that inscribes.
appearance.attire: Undyed, identical to every other guild member's and cut without a seam that could carry a signature. High collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, closed to the throat — the guild's clothing has no opening anywhere above the wrist, on the stated ground that a signature belongs on a work and never on a person. The hems are all cut at the same length by people who cannot see one another's work, and hers has been re-cut three times because she will not stop growing and nobody in the guild has ever asked her why.
appearance.marks: Nine short lines of script inside one wrist, cut on nine different dates by nine different hands, and every one of them is a name somebody put on her rather than a mark she made. She has asked for nothing to be added since the seventh and has been described, correctly, as difficult about it. The lines do not fade, do not scar, and are slightly warmer to the touch than the skin around them, which is the only part of her anybody in the guild touches.
appearance.bearing: Standing entirely still in a way that reads as composure and is in fact the absence of any mechanism that would move her — she does not fidget, does not shift, does not look away and does not lean. Three masters have described her as the calmest person they have stood beside. A fourth described the same stillness as being in a studio with something that had decided not to be a person for the afternoon.

canon.role_in_story: A guild that makes boundary art where a law used to be written re-masters its own symbols every generation, so that nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw. Its marks resolve into a figure only from a distance or in poor light, which is a property of unwritten law turned into a rule rather than left as an accident. Its teaching is conducted in gestures a listener cannot record. Its apprentices are praised only when the work has become readable and are then immediately told to break it. No member may explain a piece to an outsider, because explanation is the form of the art. Every one of those rules is a way of refusing to persist, and the generation's re-mastering is the machine that performs the refusal on schedule. Tamsin Orle is the one body in the setting that cannot be read twice: a law inscribes by writing a requirement into what it is written on, and every written account of her is exactly such an inscription, so every description of her is a different woman and no two accounts agree. The guild did not have to make anything illegible on purpose for eleven years and has not re-mastered once. That was free. What it cost is that the guild's only succession plan is now a person, and a person's plan has an end, and the guild cannot see the end coming, because the end is the one thing about her that is arithmetic rather than art. So this generation's masters have begun writing down what the teaching takes from her, in an unsteady hand, on a sheet that names nobody — the first legible artefact the guild has produced in ninety years, and it is an account of its own teacher. She has read it. She cannot tell them whether the figure is right, because telling them would be one more description, and describing her is how she is spent.
canon.first_appearance: First described, by three of the guild's own masters separately and without any of them having spoken to the others, at three different heights — and all three descriptions were entered as evidence that the apprentices had understood the marks.
canon.lore:
An unwritten is a body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe, produced when a life law runs above its authored ceiling of one, so the law has no slot in which to write the form down and the form is written anyway. Every gate it passes writes a fresh requirement into the body and the body cannot satisfy it, because its life law has no slot to hold it; the accumulated contradiction finally exceeds what any frame will bear at the twenty-ninth gate, and the thirtieth would resolve all of it at once. Nobody has returned to describe the thirtieth and the record does not speculate. It has been seen to have every organ the ladder requires and to be carrying more of each than the ladder defines. Its senses are unreliable in the exact shape of the problem — every report agrees that it perceived everything, which is what a body with no unspent capacity for interior looks like from outside. It has an inconsistency rather than a stable weakness, and an inconsistency does not behave like a weakness in a fight. It does not spread and it does not persist.

The guild she teaches is an artistic order that makes boundary art for the tiers and re-masters its own symbols every generation so that nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw. It exists because a law scar opens where a group used to be written and no longer is, and the only durable defence against a hole shaped like a discipline is an art that is always one law short of being legible. Its discipline is refusal, formally: nothing durable is made for one place; a work is finished when it would mean nothing to anyone who learned it elsewhere; no work is held past its second generation without being broken; no guild member explains a piece to an outsider; and no signature is attached to anything. Its teaching is conducted in gestures a listener cannot record. Its studios have no corner and no door, so that no interior of the guild's own making can be entered from outside by anybody reading a plan. Its diet is cold and travelling, with one dish the guild agrees on and changes every year so that no two generations are eating the same argument. It is made of the poor, the cold and the long-lived, and the lineage carrying the gift was kept in one household so long that its name stopped describing a family and started describing a body.

That is the whole of what she is to them. An unwritten cannot be read twice, and the guild's entire purpose is to be unreadable by the next generation, so it acquired, without designing it, a teacher whose presence makes the re-mastering unnecessary. For eleven years the guild has taught its symbols straight, from her, to apprentices who were never given a previous generation to unlearn, and the work has come out exactly as illegible as the discipline requires. Nobody has proposed the obvious explanation, because the obvious explanation is that the work is illegible because the teacher cannot be described, and saying that out loud is describing her. So the re-mastering stopped and the guild did not notice for four years, and what replaced it was a habit: each generation now assumes it is the second, which is not a thing the guild had ever needed to assume.

What she cannot do is see any of this. Observing her own state would be one more requirement written into a frame with no slot to hold it, so the mind path is shut for the whole reason rather than by temperament, and every judgement she makes about her own condition is reasoned from outside her own body. She has worked out the arithmetic from the guild's own materials — the marks, the standings, the dates on the festival sheets — because that is the one thing she can do that nobody else in the studio can, and she has concluded two things from it. First, that her life is the running sum of every account anybody has filed about her, and that the account the guild is now keeping of its own teacher is therefore not a record of her but a record of the guild's spending. Second, that this is the only legible thing the guild has produced in ninety years, and that it is legible in exactly the way the guild spends a generation preventing.

And there is a reason nobody can re-master out of. The guild's art and this species share a condition and were not built to share it: both are refusals to persist. The guild's is a designed property, re-mastered on a schedule, and it costs nothing. Hers is a structural one, it consumes her, and it has an end. So the guild has traded a discipline it could stop performing for a mechanism it cannot stop, and the one number in the setting that would tell them when is a number that has to be written down, which is the thing the guild does not do. There is a vocabulary in this setting for what a technique does where the law it needs is unwritten — not weaker, failing at full strength — and the honest use of it here is that the guild has been running at full strength on a requirement it never wrote for eleven years. A survey that counts what a frame has actually seated would answer honestly on her frame with a number that goes up as the subject gets stronger, which is the most precise available statement of the arrangement and the one nobody in the studio has asked for.
history: Came into being where a life's law runs above the ceiling the world was written to, so the frame accepted every gate it was offered and could satisfy none of them, and there is no record of the place because a description of the place would have been charged to her.

Reached the seventh gate without anybody teaching her, because a body that inscribes what it is told does not require instruction and does not know that it has been learning, and then stopped, and has given no account of the stopping that anybody could check, because she cannot supply her own testimony.

Was carried down off the high ground by a guild that was re-mastering its symbols and needed a teacher, and taught straight, without re-mastering, for eleven years — which is a generation's time in a craft whose whole method is that nothing may be taught straight for two.

Discovered, from the guild's own festival dates and from nothing about herself, that her life is the running sum of every account filed about her, and that the re-mastering was never a discipline she needed to teach. She has told nobody, on the reasoning that telling them is one more description and she cannot afford the last one.

Found a sheet in a master's studio with four figures on it in three different hands, all of them a count of descriptions of her, and none of them agreeing, and has established that this is the first legible artefact the guild has produced in ninety years and that it is an account of its own teacher.

personality.summary: Immense, uninspectable and entirely without a private interior, which in practice makes her the most patient teacher in the setting and not remotely a serene one. She reads materials rather than people, has no opinion about her own body that she did not infer from a document, and has developed a way of asking questions inside a lesson that four generations of apprentices have mistaken for the technique.

has not looked at her own face in four years and has not needed to, and has answered two questions about her appearance by referring the asker to the standing sheets
counts things out loud while teaching and does not know she is doing it, because the counting is the only introspection available to her and it has come out sideways
will not be praised, and has never corrected an apprentice who tried, because praise in this guild means the work has become readable

touches the inside of one wrist with the thumb of the other hand when a sheet is being signed, and the gesture has been copied by two apprentices without either of them knowing what it is
leaves a room before an apprentice can ask whether they have understood, which has been read as severity for four generations
motivations: wants the guild to re-master anyway, because the discipline is cheaper than her, and has no way to say so without spending one description
wants to be asked what she is, and has wanted that for eleven years and has never asked for it, on the arithmetic that the asking is a charge

cannot testify about herself, so every fact she holds about her own situation she holds by being told it, which in this guild means by finding a sheet
has let a craft's survival be reorganised around her without saying one word about it, which is a kindness she chose and has never examined
